evidence:
Prop:coverage (approach.tex lines 47-52) is a one-line normalisation. y = A/||A||_{1/s} is feasible for Gamma_s. The phase lemma (lem:phase, R4) is linear in A, so the bound follows. It adds nothing beyond R4 and the definition of the programme. Its novelty equals the novelty of the l_{1/s}-budgeted programme.

Closest analogue: Kam, Bessafi, Cadet, arXiv 2609.17926. I fetched the abs page and confirmed the title, authors, date (15 Sep 2026) and "under review at NeurReps 2026". The sweep notes (LIT_ml.md §0.2) report that its App. A.3.2 Eq. 15 maximises the same worst-offset coverage min_s sum_k beta_k(1-cos(omega_k s)), but under a convex l2 amplitude budget ||beta||_2 = B. Its Prop 5 finds the uniform, dense allocation optimal. The "margin <= return x budget" rescaling is implicit there too, but with exponent 2 in place of 1/s.

Morwani et al. (arXiv 2311.07568, ICLR 2024 Spotlight; confirmed) use Fourier amplitudes with a phase condition (Sec. 4) and a certificate at b = nu. They have no normalised general-s programme.
